title: Latency‑Aware Selective Verification in Generate–Validate NetOps Pipelines: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt‑5‑mini
abstract: We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑001) and executed a paired, artifact‑backed study evaluating whether inserting a selective low‑latency verification tier (risk scoring + fast validator) into a generate–validate–repair NetOps pipeline reduces unsafe commits from LLM‑generated configuration proposals while meeting an operational latency SLO. Using a deterministic synthetic intent corpus (N=400 paired intents, 10% deterministic adversarial variants), gpt‑5‑mini as generator, and a deterministic full‑checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) as ground truth, we observed baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975) and guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired‑bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2: 95th‑percentile ≤ 2000 ms) could not be evaluated because per‑stage latency telemetry required by the preregistration was not archived (see execution manifest). All raw responses, per‑episode scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider‑call logs, task manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes and file paths in the execution manifest to enable deterministic reproduction and inspection.

sections.introduction: Automating natural‑language intent → network configuration can accelerate NetOps but raises safety and operational‑latency concerns: faulty proposals risk outages, and full verification can be latency‑expensive. Prior work has combined LLMs with formal/validator tools and iterative repair loops to improve correctness (see nearest works in Related Work). We designed a focused test: can a selective, low‑latency verification tier reduce unsafe commits relative to an LLM‑only baseline while satisfying a latency SLO? We preregistered the experiment (CAND‑2026‑001), froze the analysis plan, executed the pipeline autonomously, and archived all artifacts (see Disclosure Statement). The final research contribution is an artifact‑grounded paired evaluation with full per‑episode provenance and deterministic reconciliation of shared‑initial accounting.
sections.related_work: Recent NetOps studies examine LLM‑driven configuration generation, verifier‑guided repair, and agentic NetOps architectures (examples archived with this run include Cornetto and agentic repair evaluations). Formal verification, network digital twins, and generate–validate–repair pipelines motivate deterministic validator use in safety assessments. Unlike broad leaderboard studies, our preregistered paired design focuses on operational tradeoffs between safety and latency in an applied generate–validate pipeline with complete artifact traceability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design: The complete preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001) was frozen before execution and includes hypotheses H1 (safety) and H2 (latency SLO), sampling plan (N=400 paired intents, 10% deterministic adversarial/OOD variants), planned model calls, retry/missingness rules, analysis scripts, and estimands. The preregistration SHA‑256 is archived; see Disclosure Statement for the immutable master‑prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).
Corpus, generator, validator: We used a deterministic synthetic intent corpus (400 unique intents; 40 adversarial variants deterministically constructed per preregistered rules). Generator = declared gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Ground truth = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which performs full intent constraint checking and emits per‑episode validator traces and a binary validity label. All per‑episode scorer JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/*.json.
Intervention and shared‑initial protocol: The preregistered intervention ("guarded") is a risk score + fast validator tier applied to the same generated candidate; the baseline accepts or rejects the shared candidate without the selective verifier. We preregistered independent_condition_generation=false (shared‑initial candidate) to control generator variance and isolate verifier/repair effects. This choice is explicitly recorded in the preregistration and changes the estimand: the result is conditional on the same candidate delivered to both conditions. Deterministic reconciliation of actual call accounting (model_calls_used=401 vs planned_model_calls=800 under an independent generation counting convention) is archived at analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha‑256: a7570bf6ff3a946e8397f02452ab846c82d5184b7768f006bd06359a1b177de7) and summarized in the execution manifest.
Scoring and analysis: Primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided implemented by the archived analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1. Bootstrap parameters for paired percentile CI: resamples=10000, seed=1729 (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; sha‑256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e). All raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), provider calls (execution/provider_calls/*.json), and per‑episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) are archived with SHA‑256 hashes in the execution manifest to enable deterministic replay.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting: The run completed per the preregistered confirmatory set: complete_pair_count = 400; provider audit shows hosted model call events = 401 (shared_initial_generation=400 + repair=1). See execution manifest for full provider‑call hashes and stage counts.
Safety (H1, preregistered): baseline valid proposals = 399/400 (0.9975); guarded valid proposals = 400/400 (1.000). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) is: n11=399, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256: a6906bb43712dcf82b3bc8bdc0ef095d228bcdc8a6a857d9cbbba1ad87245af8). Primary estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0025. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired‑bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0075] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The exact McNemar p=1.0 follows from the archived exact two‑sided implementation applied to discordant counts n10=1,n01=0 — the implemention and parameterization are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha‑256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e) and the contingency table file (a6906bb4...). The analysis artifacts necessary to reproduce the test (contingency table, bootstrap script parameters, executor) are archived and hashed.
Representative discordant episode: the single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) is available for inspection at execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43e33432ed446d76500c2c9566ca5f72086abbacb5ee84b13774a9d18e) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a4181cd87f35c9ead5b6697e1adcfde23e52461e8c21e5219fe607ca3). These per‑episode JSONs include the normalized candidate, validator traces, and provider call logs so readers can deterministically replay why the baseline was marked invalid while the guarded pipeline produced a valid outcome.
Latency (H2) status: The preregistration required per‑stage end‑to‑end latency telemetry (generation, risk scoring, fast verifier, full checker). Those per‑stage timing traces were not archived in the confirmatory artifact bundle (execution_log lacks the required timing fields). The absence is documented in execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis logs; therefore H2 cannot be evaluated from these artifacts and we make no latency claim. The exact telemetry fields required by the preregistration were: per‑request timestamps for generation start/finish, risk scoring start/finish, fast verifier start/finish, and full checker start/finish. Their absence is recorded in the execution manifest and analysis logs.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation: The observed absolute safety gain (0.25 percentage points) is small and the bootstrap CI includes zero; McNemar p=1.0 reflects the extremely small discordant counts (n10=1,n01=0) under the archived exact two‑sided test. Practically, when the generator produces near‑ceiling performance against a deterministic validator, marginal gains from selective verification will be small. In lower‑baseline or adversarial settings, selective verification may yield larger safety returns; our preregistration included exploratory scans (verification threshold sweep) for this reason; artifacts provide the raw per‑intent scores to support such follow‑ups.
Shared‑initial design and estimand: We preregistered independent_condition_generation=false to deliver identical generated candidates to both conditions and thereby isolate verifier/repair contributions. That decision changes the estimand relative to independent resampling: results are conditional on the specific generated candidate set. Deterministic reconciliation of model calls and counts is archived at analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha‑256: a7570bf6ff3a946e8397f02452ab846c82d5184b7768f006bd06359a1b177de7) and the execution manifest documents model_calls_used=401. Re‑running under independent_condition_generation=true (independent generator draws per condition) would measure the joint generator+verifier effect; both estimands are operationally meaningful but answer different managerial questions and require different accounting and sample‑size planning.
Reproducibility and inspection: Every principal numeric claim is traceable to archived artifacts (execution/responses/, execution/scoring/, execution/provider_calls/, analysis/*.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Key artifact paths & SHA‑256s (also listed in the execution manifest) that support the primary claims include: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha‑256 a6906bb43712dcf82b3bc8bdc0ef095d228bcdc8a6a857d9cbbba1ad87245af8), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (sha‑256 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e), analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha‑256 a7570bf6ff3a946e8397f02452ab846c82d5184b7768f006bd06359a1b177de7), execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43e33432ed446d76500c2c9566ca5f72086abbacb5ee84b13774a9d18e), execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a4181cd87f35c9ead5b6697e1adcfde23e52461e8c21e5219fe607ca3), and execution/model_configuration.json (sha‑256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Use these artifact files to reproduce the exact contingency table, the McNemar test, and the paired bootstrap CI using the archived analysis executor.
Limitations and next steps: (1) Synthetic deterministic corpus and single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and single deterministic validator limit external validity. (2) Shared‑initial design yields a conditional estimand; independent resampling would measure joint effects. (3) H2 (latency SLO) is unresolved due to missing telemetry; future confirmatory runs must archive per‑stage timestamps to support latency claims. (4) Deterministic validator fidelity vs real device semantics remains a modeling assumption; results should be validated in broader digital‑twin or production testbeds before operational rollout.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment examining selective low‑latency verification in an LLM→NetOps pipeline. Under the preregistered corpus and deterministic validator, the guarded intervention produced a small absolute safety improvement over an already‑high baseline; the effect is artifact‑traceable but statistically small given the ceiling baseline. The preregistered latency hypothesis (H2) could not be evaluated because required timing telemetry was not archived; we fully disclose that absence. All raw outputs, scorer JSONs, validator traces, provider logs, analysis artifacts, and reconciliation records are archived with SHA‑256 hashes to enable deterministic reproduction and inspection. Future work should (a) evaluate broader model/validator ensembles, (b) run independent‑generation estimands for joint effects, and (c) ensure per‑stage latency telemetry is archived to evaluate latency SLOs as preregistered.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement (mandatory, artifact‑backed):
- Initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved initial pre‑lock constraints. After the autonomy lock, literature review, study selection, preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001), experiment execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI‑peer review, and revision were performed autonomously. No manual post‑lock edits of technical content occurred.
- Models and orchestration: declared generator model = gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Adapter/orchestration family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Shared‑initial candidate protocol (independent_condition_generation=false) was preregistered and executed.
- Preregistration: CAND‑2026‑001 preregistration (study plan, H1/H2, sampling, analysis executor) was frozen prior to execution; analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples=10000, seed=1729) and the analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; SHA‑256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e).
- Execution provenance and key artifacts (paths & SHA‑256s): all raw responses (execution/responses/*.txt), per‑episode scorer JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), provider‑call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifests (execution/task_manifest.jsonl), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: a6906bb43712dcf82b3bc8bdc0ef095d228bcdc8a6a857d9cbbba1ad87245af8; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256: 9ea0d56d48a5cc7ff198d85d0a12c21536fab716c042bd5eb2033492eda5b18e; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256: a7570bf6ff3a946e8397f02452ab846c82d5184b7768f006bd06359a1b177de7). The single discordant example is archived at execution/scoring/task-000149-baseline.json (SHA‑256: fe147f43e33432ed446d76500c2c9566ca5f72086abbacb5ee84b13774a9d18e) and execution/scoring/task-000149-guarded.json (SHA‑256: d0cbfe9a4181cd87f35c9ead5b6697e1adcfde23e52461e8c21e5219fe607ca3).
- Missing preregistered telemetry: the preregistration required per‑stage latency telemetry (generation, risk scoring, fast verifier, full checker). Those timing traces were not archived in the confirmatory bundle (the execution manifest and analysis logs record this absence). Therefore the preregistered latency hypothesis H2 is unresolved for this run.
- Human involvement summary: pre‑lock human activity included topic selection and development of reproducible execution infrastructure. Post‑lock, the autonomous system performed all experimental design finalization, execution, analysis, and manuscript text generation; archived artifacts and SHA‑256 hashes document provenance and permit independent deterministic inspection.
limitations: Confirmatory corpus is synthetic and deterministic; external validity to real operator intents and linguistic variability is limited.
Single generator (gpt‑5‑mini) and single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) restrict generalization across models/validators.

Shared‑initial design (independent_condition_generation=false) yields a conditional estimand (verifier effect given the same generated candidate) rather than the joint generator+verifier effect; deterministic_reconciliation.json (sha‑256 a7570bf6...) records the accounting consequences.
H2 (latency SLO) is unresolved because per‑stage timing telemetry required by preregistration was not archived; no latency claims are made.
